claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child. I have one child - Alex, who is 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 19 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether they are still in approved education or training. Child Benefit usually stops when a child turns 16, but can continue until their 20th birthday if they remain in qualifying education or approved training.

Could you tell me if Alex is currently in any of the following:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or equivalent)
- Approved training (such as a traineeship in England, or certain programmes in Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know, thank you. A-levels count as qualifying education for Child Benefit purposes.

Now I need to ask a few more questions about your circumstances:

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care, such as providing food, clothing, and accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am responsible for his day-to-day care - I provide his food, clothing, and accommodation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

Are you (or your spouse/partner, if applicable) a UK resident, and do you have the right to live in the UK? This includes being a British or Irish citizen, or having settled or pre-settled status, or having the right to work in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and I'm a UK resident with the right to live here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 19 years old
- He is studying A-levels (which is approved education)
- He lives with you
- You are responsible for his day-to-day care
- You are a UK resident with the right to live in the UK

Let me confirm my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex:**
- Although Alex is 19, Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 (up to their 20th birthday) as long as they remain in approved education or training
- A-levels count as approved non-advanced education
- You meet all other requirements: you're a UK resident with the right to live here, Alex lives with you, and you're responsible for his day-to-day care

**Important to note:**
- You'll continue to be eligible as long as Alex stays in approved education
- Eligibility will end when Alex turns 20 or finishes his A-levels (whichever comes first)
- You would need to inform the Child Benefit Office if Alex's circumstances change (for example, if he starts working 24+ hours per week or leaves education)

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
